lines.en: P is the cone apex; O is the base center.
AB is a diameter of length 2.
Part 1: PA makes an angle of pi over 3 with the base.
Find the lateral surface area.
Part 2: Q is the midpoint of the generator PA.
C and D lie on the base circle.
Arc AC has length pi over 3.
CD is parallel to AB.
T moves along segment OC.
Prove that QT is parallel to plane PBD.
The radius is OA = AB/2 = 1.
PO is perpendicular to the base; PA projects onto AO.
Thus angle PAO is pi over 3, or 60 degrees.
Since cos 60 degrees = OA/PA, the slant height PA is 2.
The lateral area is pi times radius times slant height: 2 pi.
In the top view, arc length divided by radius gives 60 degrees.
Draw OM perpendicular to CD. Then CM = MD.
Since CD is parallel to AB, angle OCM equals angle COA: 60 degrees.
CM = OC cos 60 degrees = 1/2, so CD = 1.
CD and OB are parallel and have equal lengths.
OCDB is a parallelogram, so OC is parallel to BD.
Return to the spatial view and join OQ.
In triangle PAB, O and Q are the midpoints of AB and AP.
The midpoint theorem gives OQ parallel to BP.
Together with OC parallel to BD, two intersecting pairs are parallel.
The plane parallelism criterion gives plane QOC parallel to plane PBD.
As T lies on OC, line QT lies in plane QOC.
The planes are disjoint, so QT is parallel to plane PBD.
Part 1: find the projection and slant height. The area is 2 pi.
Part 2: combine the base geometry with the midpoint theorem.
For every T on OC, QT is parallel to plane PBD.
